questions.key_step: H, G, C collinear in ratio 2:1; compare coefficients.
questions.justification: One Euler-line relation then coefficient comparison; 2-3 routine steps, options available.

questions.key_step: Two cross products, then projection formula.
questions.justification: Chain of three routine computations; the triple-product shortcut is optional.

questions.key_step: Bisector direction is $\hat a+\hat b$; distance via cross product.
questions.justification: Three routine steps (bisector, distance, |2a-1|=9); no insight beyond the standard formulas.

questions.key_step: Components along/perpendicular to $\vec b$ identify $\vec a$.
questions.justification: Short chain: dot product, subtraction, add squares; direct once the decomposition is recalled.

questions.key_step: $(\vec a+\vec b)\times\vec c=0$ so $\vec c\parallel\vec a+\vec b$.
questions.justification: One neat rewriting then a quadratic in $\lambda$ and a max; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Perpendicularity conditions give two linear equations for the feet.
questions.justification: Standard skew-line procedure with two linear equations and an option test; routine but long.

questions.key_step: Height of the triangle is the distance from B to the line.
questions.justification: One familiar move (foot of perpendicular), a short calculation.

questions.key_step: Equate two parametrisations of lines to find the intersection.
questions.justification: One familiar move, direct arithmetic.

questions.key_step: Equidistance gives linear equations; sides decide both statements.
questions.justification: Solve for the point, then two statements each needing a short check.

questions.key_step: Direction is $\vec d_1\times\vec d_2$ and the given linear form is constant on the plane of $L_1,L_3$.
questions.justification: The final quantity is only constant through a non-obvious cancellation; the required observation is less familiar.

questions.key_step: Foot of perpendicular and intersection point, both on $L$.
questions.justification: Two parameters found from standard conditions then a distance.

questions.key_step: Two linear angle conditions plus unit length give a quadratic with two roots; only one matches the options.
questions.justification: A longer chain with two roots and a check against options; extra precision risk.

questions.key_step: Solve for $x$ from $\vec a\cdot\vec d=1,|\vec d|=1$, then triple product.
questions.justification: Direct two-stage computation.

questions.key_step: $\vec a=\vec b\times\vec c$ gives $\vec a\perp\vec c$ and $|\vec c|\sin\alpha=\frac23$; minimise.
questions.justification: Two ideas linked (perpendicularity, then monotonic minimisation over the angle range).

questions.key_step: Quadratic in $|\vec c|$ from $|\vec c-\vec a|$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec c$; the constraint $|\vec c|\ge6$ selects the root.
questions.justification: Several linked conditions (dot, magnitude, cross product, angle) with a root selection.

questions.key_step: $x=\gamma\sin\phi\cos\theta$ and distance $\sqrt{\gamma^2-x^2}$.
questions.justification: Direction-cosine relations chained; no real insight.

questions.key_step: Scale factor $k$ eliminated between two conditions gives a linear equation in $\lambda$.
questions.justification: Routine chain of dot products and one elimination.

questions.key_step: Area $=\tfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|$ gives a quadratic in $\alpha$.
questions.justification: Cross product, square, solve; routine.

questions.key_step: Lagrange's identity for Statement I; circumcentre-vector argument for Statement II.
questions.justification: Two statements, each needing a genuine check, one a less familiar trigonometric inequality.

questions.key_step: Area from diagonals, then integer solutions of $\alpha^2+5\beta^2=29$ with $\alpha\beta=-6$.
questions.justification: Cross product, algebra, small integer search; routine.
